solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Amend florid clothing that overlaps

indicators.note: two words that overlap share a letter where they meet, so the doubled letter is written only once

blocks.note: florid means ruddy in complexion
to dress is to clothe; dress is clothing

explanation.surface: A request to correct someone's over-ornate outfit where the layers overlap.
explanation.walkthrough: RED DRESS has a D at the end of one word and the start of the next; overlapping them gives REDRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to put it right, a direct synonym of amend as a verb.

clue.text: Comedian visiting relative to obtain family tree above all

indicators.note: to obtain is to get hold of, so those pieces take another inside them
in a down entry, placed above everything else means written first

blocks.note: the rowan is the mountain ash
visiting a place is being at it
kin are one's family
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: A comedian calls on a relative to look up the family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To obtain' means the visiting and relative pieces close around the family piece; 'above all' puts the tree on top because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowan Atkinson is the British comic actor famous as Mr Bean and Blackadder.

clue.text: Party involving scrap on drive

indicators.note: to involve is to include, so one word includes the other inside it

blocks.note: a do is a party
a rag is a scrap of cloth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party features a fight while on a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight but means a rag; 'drive' suggests motoring but is a verb meaning force.
explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon someone is to coerce them into doing something, to drive or force them.

clue.text: Wipe out insurgent in Bruges area

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the following words, spanning their join
an insurgent rises up, and rising in a down entry means reading upwards

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Destroying a rebel in a Belgian city's district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insurgent' looks like a person to be wiped out, but signals reading the letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete completely.

clue.text: Mum eggs on bigwig to leave quickly

blocks.note: mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence
O looks like an egg, so eggs are OO
joins the pieces in order
a toff is a posh, upper-class person

explanation.surface: A mother urges an important person to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not a mother but the word for keeping quiet. Toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot off is an informal phrasal verb meaning to depart in a hurry.

clue.text: Make small dumpling when empty

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: dumpling is an informal word for a dim, dumpy person, as dodo is for a dullard
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: shape the dumplings small when the bowl is empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone down is to belittle them, which is to make them seem small.

clue.text: Wanderer touring Spain lifted spirit

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go around it, so one word circles the other
lifted means raised up, and reading upwards in a down entry turns the letters round

blocks.note: a nomad wanders without a fixed home
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A traveller going round Spain is cheered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted spirit' reads as a mood improving, but spirit alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A daemon is a supernatural being or attendant spirit in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Paint detective capturing current mood

indicators.note: capturing someone means holding them inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: DS is a detective sergeant
I is the symbol for electric current
temper means mood or humour

explanation.surface: A painter detective catches the spirit of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: DS holds the current symbol, then TEMPER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a water-based paint once widely used on walls and scenery.

clue.text: Successive characters in despair initially dyeing fabric

indicators.note: one piece sits in another that wraps around it
initially points at the first letter of the word beside it

blocks.note: woe is deep distress
three consecutive letters of the alphabet
its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone in despair as each letter dyes a cloth in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Successive characters' means any run of consecutive alphabet letters; the despair word tells you which run fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Worsted is a smooth woollen cloth made from long-staple combed yarn.

clue.text: Arcade game completely captivating Bill (American)

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so one word holds the others inside it

blocks.note: whole means complete, in its entirety
AC is short for account, a bill
standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill, an American, is utterly hooked on an arcade machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is an account; the brackets keep American as a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Whac-A-Mole is the coin-operated amusement where players hammer plastic moles as they pop up.

clue.text: Musical genre introduced by singular child

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
prog is progressive rock

explanation.surface: A single child gets someone into a style of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduced by' puts the singular letter in front. Sprog is British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is informal British slang for a young child or baby.

clue.text: US writer's lodger spending half time with robust mug of beer

indicators.note: having spent half, only the other half of the word remains

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
in rude health means robust
a stein is a German beer mug

explanation.surface: An American author's lodger passes time hearty with a beer mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude Stein was the American modernist writer who hosted a famous Paris salon.

clue.text: Smell maintains focus of boa constrictor

indicators.note: to maintain is to keep or hold, so one word holds another within it
the focus is the central point, so only the middle letter of the following word counts

blocks.note: a wine's nose is its smell
the middle letter of the snake's name

explanation.surface: A natural history note about how a boa locates its prey by scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boa constrictor' reads as the snake, but boa only lends a letter and constrictor alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose tightens around the neck, so it is literally something that constricts.

clue.text: Proverbial company car Edgar unloaded — like this type?

indicators.note: unloaded means emptied of contents, so only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: the proverb says two's company, three's a crowd
SEAT is a Spanish car maker
the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: A company car meant for Edgar alone is cleared out, inviting the question of what sort of car it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at the clue: a car for a company of two is a two-seater.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-seater is a small car with room for just a driver and one passenger, the type the clue describes.

clue.text: Island's paper money bank recounted

indicators.note: to recount is to tell, so these words are judged by how they sound when spoken

blocks.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note
a reef is a bank of rock or sand in the sea

explanation.surface: An island's banknotes and bank are described.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, tenner and reef make the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife is the largest of Spain's Canary Islands.

clue.text: Get angry with flash champion blocking volley

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits in the middle of it

blocks.note: a volley or rain of blows
in a flash means in a second, abbreviated SEC
A1 means first-rate, the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A champion loses temper with a fancy rival who stops a volley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' here is the adjective sense, first-rate, written as A1 with the digit standing in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise Cain is an idiom for making a loud angry fuss, from the biblical murderer.

clue.text: Is it taking residence around sink, getting a recoil?

definitions.text: Is it taking residence around sink, getting a recoil?

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it
a recoil springs back, so the built letters run backwards

blocks.note: RES is the abbreviation for residence
to sink is to dip

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a creature living around the sink makes people recoil.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a creature lurking round the sink that makes people jump back.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders famously lurk around bathroom sinks and plugholes, making people jump back in fright.

clue.text: Female entertained by style of jazz pianist? One could get hooked

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within the host's home

blocks.note: in the manner of Thelonious Monk, the jazz pianist
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman enjoys a pianist's style and admits it is addictive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooked' suggests addiction, but it means caught on a fishing hook.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkfish is a sea fish caught by anglers and trawlers, so it can be hooked.

clue.text: Having problems with present regulars in Mayfair spot

indicators.note: regulars are evenly spaced, so every second letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: to be in is to be present, at home
the second, fourth and sixth letters
X marks the spot on a map

explanation.surface: Someone is in difficulty choosing a gift for regular customers at a smart London spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an expensive district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a fix is an idiom for being in trouble or a difficult situation.

clue.text: A barrier enclosing PC World's alarm

indicators.note: to enclose is to surround, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a gate is a barrier
the world of PCs is information technology

explanation.surface: A security barrier around a computer store is setting off an alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: PC World is a British computer retail chain, but here it just means the field of computing.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to disturb or alarm someone, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Voracious foreign correspondent, say, in extremities of Greenland

indicators.note: one part sits in the other, which wraps around it
extremities are the far ends, so only the first and last letters count

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the name
a foreign correspondent is 'our man in' some city, as in Our Man in Havana

explanation.surface: A hungry reporter abroad is stationed at the edges of Greenland.
explanation.walkthrough: G and D wrap OUR MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a greedy eater, so used adjectivally it means gluttonous.

clue.text: Filling publication with priest looking heavenwards?

indicators.note: looking up the column of a down entry means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: mag is short for magazine
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A magazine article about a priest gazing up to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling' looks like padding but is the dental sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Amalgam is the mercury alloy dentists use to fill teeth.

clue.text: Man in navy and brown pattern

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor
tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: A man dressed in navy blue and brown with a pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Navy' looks like a colour beside brown, but man in navy is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is the Scottish checked pattern of crossing coloured stripes.

clue.text: Image with old king, during pillage, that's holding mace?

indicators.note: something happening during another event falls within it, so these pieces go inside

blocks.note: to sack a town is to plunder it
pic is short for picture
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A picture of an ancient king amid looting, holding a ceremonial club.
explanation.walkthrough: Mace looks like the weapon or ceremonial staff, but it is the spice made from nutmeg husks.
explanation.definitionFit: A spice rack is a kitchen shelf holding jars of spices, such as mace.

clue.text: Dave's partner engaging Peugeot's first gear

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so one word holds the other
first points at the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: Chas & Dave were a London pop duo
the opening letter of the car brand

explanation.surface: One half of a musical duo puts a French car into first gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' looks like the car's gear, but it is clothing; chaps are leather leg-coverings worn over trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaps are protective leather leggings, an item of riding gear or clothing.

clue.text: Pass middle of zone where irrigation sometimes done

indicators.note: the middle means the central letters, with both ends discarded

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass
the two central letters

explanation.surface: A route through a mountain zone where fields are watered.
explanation.walkthrough: Irrigation suggests farmland, but here it is colonic irrigation, a medical cleansing.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonic irrigation flushes the large intestine, so the colon is where it takes place.

clue.text: Flipping amateur disturbs an antelope

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word runs backwards
something that disturbs breaks into another, sitting inside it

blocks.note: taken as written; it wraps around
lay means non-professional, amateur

explanation.surface: An incompetent amateur startles an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild curse but turns the amateur word round.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Hearing Victor's excluded from latest conversation on Zoom?

indicators.note: something excluded is left out, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a court hearing is a trial
Victor is V in the NATO alphabet
the latest fashion is the vogue

explanation.surface: A court hearing where the winner was shut out of the most recent online call.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a video call may well have three participants.
explanation.definitionFit: A trialogue is a discussion among three people, as might happen in a video meeting.

clue.text: Check on homes

blocks.note: re means on, concerning
to be in is to be at home, so two homes give two INs

explanation.walkthrough: Short clue reading like a house inspection; homes is plural, so its word appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or curb, which is to check as a verb.

clue.text: An arm and a leg laid out for this game?

definitions.text: An arm and a leg laid out for this game?

blocks.clueFragment: An arm and a leg laid out
blocks.note: surface reading: paying a fortune, an arm and a leg, for something
setter's reading: limbs drawn one by one on a gallows figure in a word-guessing game played on paper

explanation.walkthrough: 'An arm and a leg' is the idiom for a high price, but here it means the stick figure's limbs drawn after each wrong guess.
explanation.definitionFit: In the pencil game each wrong letter adds a body part to a figure on a gallows until it is complete.
